findings.title: The pairing ratio is taken on trust from the minter's registered `decimals`; the dangerous direction fails OPEN and is permissionlessly exploitable

findings.rootCause: Antimatter computes its entire economic premise from `decimals` read out of PhusdStableMinter.stablecoinConfigs, a value registerStablecoin accepts verbatim and never checks against IERC20Metadata(stablecoin).decimals(). Antimatter performs no independent check although it holds the token address and could do so in one staticcall.
findings.asymmetry: decimals OVERSTATED (6-dp registered as 18): scale collapses to 1, pull is 1e12x too large, safeTransferFrom reverts on balance - fails CLOSED, harmless. decimals UNDERSTATED (18-dp registered as 6): scale becomes 1e12, the pull collapses by 1e12x, BOTH contracts make the same error so it cancels inside calculateMintAmount and nothing reverts - fails OPEN, silently, at full phUSD issuance.
findings.impact: Any antimatter holder can permissionlessly receive 200 phUSD per 100 AM while surrendering 1e8 raw units (1e-10) of the stablecoin. The stable leg of phUSD - the leg that is supposed to be fully collateralised - becomes backed by dust, for as long as the misconfiguration stands and for as much antimatter as exists. No revert, no event anomaly, no on-chain signal; the :230 residue check and :233 non-zero receipt both pass.
findings.footgunTest: Law 3 - an owner mis-typing one decimals argument would expect a revert or a proportionally wrong ratio, NOT a silent unbounded permissionless free-mint. Surprise => footgun => in scope.

findings.title: Half of every annihilation's phUSD is minted against no incoming value, and the resulting liability is unbounded, unscheduled and unrecorded
findings.mergeAction: ECON-001 and FAITH-002 COLLAPSED INTO ONE. Justification below.
findings.econFaithMergeJustification: FAITH-002 and ECON-001 are the same defect at the same line (:236) with the same root cause (an unbacked mint whose size is unbounded) and the SAME mitigation (bound emission at src/Antimatter.sol:179 / account for the liability). FAITH-002's own text instructs 'Deduplicate against econ-scanner's finding on the same mint at :236 - econ owns the impact sizing'. Its distinct contribution is a QUALIFIER, not a separate remediation: it records that the behaviour is INTENDED, not accidental (Law-1 overriding Law-2 on a faithfully-implemented but unsafe intent). A qualifier with no separate fix does not earn a second submission - it is preserved as `specStatus` inside this entry, and the entry is dual-channelled to spec-conformance so the faithfulness report still carries it. CONTRAST: FAITH-001 is NOT merged here (see DEDUP-015) because 'the written justification is false' has a different root cause (documentation defect), a different remediation (correct the NatSpec), and lands on a different reader (integrators), and because collapsing it would let the doc defect vanish if the econ finding is ever triaged as accepted-by-design.
findings.specStatus: FAITHFUL-BUT-UNSAFE. Law-1 override on Law-2: the declared intent ('this contract mints the phUSD for the antimatter half', :188-189; CLAUDE.md 'antimatter's entire value to a holder is that it annihilates into phUSD worth twice its quantity') is implemented exactly. The intent itself is the hazard. Filed as a spec-level rather than implementation-level security finding.
findings.rootCause: Antimatter.mint (:179) has no cap, schedule, or tie to yield or collateral; :236 mints exactly `amount` phUSD against nothing but the burn of a token that was itself minted for free. No contract anywhere tracks the resulting unbacked supply.
findings.economicImpact: Each outstanding antimatter token is a permanent, exercisable, $1-denominated call on the phUSD collateral pool. Fair value max(0, 2p-1); at p=$1 emitting N antimatter is economically identical to writing an $N cheque against phUSD's backing. phUSD has no redemption path, so this never becomes on-chain insolvency - it becomes peg pressure, and the cash loss lands on whatever protocol-owned liquidity absorbs the annihilator's sell.

steps: Receive N antimatter free as a staking reward (:180)
Acquire N (rescaled) stablecoin at ~$1 - real capital
annihilateFrom(stable,self,self,N): burn N AM, surrender $N stable, receive ~2N phUSD (:236-237)
Sell 2N phUSD into protocol-owned liquidity at price p
Net = 2Np - N; profitable for all p > 0.5
profitableLoop.profitability: 100% return per cycle at p=$1.00, capital-recycling, permissionless, no flash loan. Keeps paying arbitrageurs until phUSD reaches half peg.
profitableLoop.notAnAtomicAttack: annihilation is one-way; the attacker must actually hold antimatter and actually part with stablecoin. This is why it is Medium, not High.

evidence.invariantQuantification: invariant_04 PASSES as an EXACT equality over 76,800 calls in both decimal regimes: phUSD.totalSupply() minus stablecoin in custody (18dp-normalised) == cumulative antimatter burned. The pass is not an all-clear - it is the measurement that the uncollateralised leg is exactly 1:1 with antimatter burned, no rounding drift. invariant_05 separately confirms every stablecoin unit pulled reached strategy custody.
evidence.scopeLimit: invariants 04/05 pin exchangeRate at 1e18; rate divergence is DEDUP-005's territory.

findings.severityRationale: C4 Medium ('value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements'). NOT High: no assets stolen from a specific victim by a specific attack path, no redemption to fail, nothing bricks, and the multiplier itself is documented intent. NOT Low: the liability is real, permanent, unbounded, lands on parties who never consented, and no on-chain control or even observation of it exists.
findings.escalationTrigger: If antimatter emission is ever wired to a permissionless or high-volume minter via setApprovedMinter (:151), re-weigh as High. See parked PARK-003 - antimatter is not yet wired into phoenix-phase-2-staging, so emission policy is entirely undecided on-chain.

findings.title: exchangeRate re-prices only the stable leg: a hard 1x issuance floor no setting can go below, an unbounded ceiling, and a silent re-scaling of what maxMintPerDay permits
findings.mergeAction: 3-way consolidation. AM-LOCAL-005 is the profiler's local half ('unbounded owner parameter'), MR-05 is the code-scanner's parked deferral of the same lever, ECON-003 supplies the operator-lever model. All three cite the rate-independence of :254-256 and :236. ECON-003 itself states 'that entry records the local half; this one adds the operator-lever model'.
findings.rootCause: The stablecoin PULLED is rate-independent (decimals only) and the antimatter leg is always exactly `amount`; only the stable leg's phUSD is rate-scaled. Total issuance per unit of stablecoin received is (1 + exchangeRate/1e18). Antimatter applies no sanity bound of its own even though it already reads the config struct at :250.
findings.impact: (a) THROTTLE FLOOR: the natural response to over-issuance is to lower the rate, but at rate=0.10e18 the protocol still emits 1.10 phUSD per $1 taken in, and the unbacked component is completely unaffected. There is no rate that makes annihilation backing-neutral; the only lever that stops dilution is setStablecoinEnabled(false) - a full stop with no intermediate setting. (b) AMPLIFIER: at rate=1.5e18 the pair emits 2.5 phUSD per $1, from a single unbounded, un-timelocked owner call.
findings.interactionWithDedup002: Changing the rate silently re-scales the effective daily cap: at rate 0.5e18 the effective maxMintPerDay multiplier moves from 2x to 3x the entered number. Two knobs interacting in a direction neither is documented to move.
findings.footgunTest: Law 3 - surprise on both counts: that lowering the rate cannot bring issuance to parity, and that changing the rate silently re-scales what maxMintPerDay permits. Neither is documented on either side. In scope.
findings.safeConfigGuidance: Treat exchangeRate as an amplitude control on the BACKED leg only, never as an issuance throttle. Keep it at or below 1e18 on every annihilatable stablecoin. Recompute maxMintPerDay as intendedIssuance / (1 + exchangeRate/1e18) on every rate change. To actually stop dilution use setStablecoinEnabled(false).

evidence.symbolic: halmos PROVED (tier3/halmos-p2-noresidue-unbounded.txt) the no-residue property holds for EVERY uint256 exchangeRate - i.e. an arbitrary rate does not strand assets. The hazard is economic, not a settlement defect, which this proof isolates.
evidence.profitabilityBoundary: the annihilator's loop (DEDUP-004) stays profitable whenever p > 1/(1 + rate/1e18): p > $1.00 at rate 0, p > $0.50 at rate 1e18.

recommendation: Add a sanity bound in Antimatter itself - it already reads exchangeRate's sibling fields at :250 and can assert mintedForStable is within tolerance of `amount`, so a fat-fingered or oversized rate fails closed.
Alternatively scale the antimatter leg by the same rate at :236 so the single knob governs the whole output.

findings.title: Annihilation and ordinary phUSD minting share one daily budget, and the annihilation path extracts 2x per unit of budget - griefing the on-ramp is the most profitable use of it
findings.mergeAction: KEPT SEPARATE from DEDUP-002. Verified before deciding: both concern PhusdStableMinter's maxMintPerDay counter, but the root causes differ - DEDUP-002 is 'the counter under-counts issuance by 2x', DEDUP-006 is 'the counter is a shared budget an annihilator can profitably exhaust'. Different impact class (availability/DoS vs mis-sized rail), different mitigation (separate budget per path + fixed epoch boundary vs charging the AM leg). Collapsing them would bury the DoS.
findings.rootCause: PhusdStableMinter.mint is the protocol's general permissionless phUSD on-ramp; Antimatter routes through the identical function and charges the same config.mintedToday. An ordinary minter gets 1 phUSD per unit of budget; an annihilator gets 2.
findings.impact: Denial of the protocol's ordinary stablecoin->phUSD on-ramp for a given stablecoin for the remainder of a 24h window, achieved by a party who is PAID ~$1 per unit for doing it. Cost of the DoS is zero - it is a side effect of a profitable trade. The window-reset semantics (restart on the first mint after expiry, not on a fixed schedule) additionally let the annihilator control when each window opens.
affectedParties: any downstream protocol path that mints phUSD through PhusdStableMinter
findings.assumptionGap: Bites only when maxMintPerDay is non-zero; registerStablecoin defaults it to 0 = unlimited. If the operator never sets a cap, DEDUP-006 is inert and DEDUP-002 is moot - but then there is no issuance rate limit at all, which is DEDUP-004.
recommendation: Give the annihilation path its own budget, or charge the antimatter leg too (which also fixes DEDUP-002) so the two paths consume budget proportionally to what they issue.
Use a fixed epoch boundary to remove the first-minter timing control.
findings.severityRationale: C4 Medium: protocol function/availability impacted. Not High: no theft, self-resolving each window, and only bites when maxMintPerDay is set non-zero.

findings.rootCause: The stable leg's phUSD is sized from `amount`, never from what the yield strategy actually credited. PhusdStableMinter makes a bare statement call to IYieldStrategy.deposit and discards its return. Antimatter's post-conditions cannot catch a shortfall: :230 asserts only that the stablecoin LEFT Antimatter, :232-233 measures a phUSD delta and requires it merely to be non-zero.

diffEvidence.pinnedTree: lib/phUSD-stable-minter/lib/vault @ 043ff2c - IYieldStrategy.sol:15 declares deposit(address,uint256,address) with NO return. Against this tree the discard is correct and there is no finding.
diffEvidence.masterTree: vault master 0110ce4 - IYieldStrategy.sol:24 declares `... returns (uint256 creditedPrincipal)`, introduced by stories 043/044/048/049 precisely because conservative ERC4626 crediting can credit strictly LESS than `amount`.
diffEvidence.abiImpact: NONE - the selector depends on argument types only and Solidity ignores surplus returndata, so a master-tree strategy does not brick the call; it silently succeeds while the shortfall goes unrecorded. That silence is what makes this worth filing.

findings.specText: 'no new entry point that reaches _burn except annihilateFrom' ... 'test_noPublicBurnEntryPoints in test/Annihilation.t.sol is a trip-wire for this rule.' (lib/antimatter/CLAUDE.md)
findings.deviation: The test asserts that four hardcoded selectors revert: burn(uint256), burn(address,uint256), burnFrom(address,uint256), annihilate(address,uint256). It cannot detect what the rule prohibits - ANY new entry point reaching _burn - because a burn path under any other name is simply not in the list and the test passes green. Two further gaps: the rule also names 'no transfer to address(0) path' and 'no owner-callable clawback', and neither is probed at all (transfer-to-zero happens to be closed by OpenZeppelin's _update, i.e. by the base class, not by anything this repo asserts).
findings.encodingDefect: All four signatures are encoded with two arguments (abi.encodeWithSignature(signatures[i], user, 1 ether)), so the one-argument burn(uint256) probe passes trailing calldata the decoder ignores - it would decode amount = uint256(uint160(user)) = 2827 wei rather than 1 ether. It would still catch a naive burn(uint256), but only because the address literal happens to be a small non-zero number. The probe is not testing what it reads as testing.
findings.invariantHoldsAt0bb82d8: YES. src/Antimatter.sol contains exactly one _burn (:215, inside annihilateFrom) and one _mint (:180, onlyApprovedMinters). findings.recommendation: Replace the name-denylist with a property assertion (totalSupply is non-decreasing across every non-annihilateFrom external call, exercised by fuzzed calldata) or a source assertion (a single _burn occurrence, inside annihilateFrom).
